summary.name: Enpass
summary.one_liner: Enpass is a password and passkey manager that stores encrypted vault data in the customer's own Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace environment rather than on Enpass servers.
use_cases: store passwords and passkeys across devices
share account access within a team
keep credential data inside company Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace
meet compliance and data residency requirements
manage business password policies and audit logs
summary.what_it_does: Enpass manages passwords, passkeys, cards and files in encrypted vaults. The page says the encrypted data lives in the customer's own Microsoft 365, Google Workspace or other trusted environment, and that Enpass never receives or stores the credential data. Encryption is described as AES-256 with 320,000 PBKDF2 rounds using the open-source SQLCipher engine, and the company states it has been independently audited. Business tiers add administrative controls, policy enforcement, audit logs, SSO, SCIM provisioning, MDM deployment and SIEM integration. The page lists Personal, Enterprise and Business plans, with a free-tier limit of 25 items in one vault.
notable: Data stored in customer's own Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace, not vendor servers
Claims zero possession: vendor never receives or stores credential data
Business tier adds SCIM provisioning, SSO, SIEM integration and audit logs
Listed on the awesome-mac list under Password Management
caveats: Free tier is limited to 25 items in one vault; full features require a paid plan
Business pricing shown is discounted first-year pricing; additional enterprise benefits require contacting sales
Marketing claims such as 'no mass breach risk' and 'only solution' are vendor assertions on the page
